title: Node-dedup is a first-class judge capability (dup-cluster queue, cosine 0.80 recall + agent precision)
summary: Generalized the edge-judge to NODE adjudication. lib/judge.js gains dupClusters(overlay,threshold=0.80,cap=8): union-find over CURRENT vec'd notes by pairwise cosine, returns size>=2 clusters (cap trims blobs to densest core). buildQueue/judgeQueueDepth add a third 'dup-cluster' bucket, watermarked in overlay.judgedClusters by a stable signature (sorted keys) + epoch. /judge/verdict gains consolidate{keep,supersede[],why} (supersedeNote stamps validTo non-destructively, THEN re-points context edges off superseded notes onto keeper, dedups, drops self-loops) and surfaceCluster{keys,why} (ONE cluster-level guidance item). Retired pairwise surfaceSupersede. KEY FINDING: no single cosine cut reproduces ground truth — true dups span cosine 0.55-0.87, so 0.70 over-merges into a 21-note blob (pair-precision 0.07) and 0.84 misses dups (recall 0.30). 0.80 is the RECALL bar (prec 0.50/recall 0.55, max cluster 5, no blob); the AGENT supplies precision, exactly the RAG-recall-then-adjudicate architecture. Dogfood: 113 pairwise guidance items -> cleared; 8 clusters auto-consolidated, 10 notes superseded (151->141 current), 11 context edges re-pointed, 0 dangling edges to hidden notes; 2 genuinely-distinct benchmark series surfaced (NOT merged); reversibility proven via /search?asOf. All 29 test suites green.
